doc.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Alfred Laine Interview, 1951-04-21

title: Original Dixieland Jazz Band, New Orleans Rhythm Kings, Brown and Shields
summary: Jack says those bands were named after the record dates, that he put together players for such dates, and that he picked up Tom Brown and Harry Shields as small boys.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: I have one or two more words. Jack, many records that the collectors are saving now have been made by two bands, one called the Original Dixieland Jazz Band, and the other one, the New Orleans Rhythm Kings. It's my impression that these were both makeshift bands whose name was coined for the record date. Is that so, or did they exist beforehand? No, that was after the record date. They didn't play together as groups before then? No. Did you ever get different ones and put them together for a date like that?
I sure did, lots of them.
I see. Now, another thing, too. Do you remember Tom Brown and Harry Shields when they used to play in the old days?
Yes, I do remember. I picked them boys up playing with me when they were just small children.
